newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, May 3 and April 26 Initial Claims from 347,000; May 3 4-week average from 336,250 and April 26 from 330,500; and April 26 from Continued Claims from 2,315,000 and April 19 from 2,249,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 340,000 in the May 10 week.
Labor said seven states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended May 3, the latest period for which data are available.
They were Michigan, with 4,412 fewer claims; North Dakota, with 4,240; Massachusetts, with 3,429; Louisiana, with 1,994; Ohio, with 1,809; Connecticut, with 1,128; and New Jersey, with 1,085.
Michigan had fewer layoffs in various industries, New Jersey reported fewer layoffs in the trade and service industries, while a majority of North Dakota's fewer claims were flood related.
Massachusetts, Louisiana, Ohio and Connecticut had no comment.
Labor said five states and one territory reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the May 3 week.
They were New York, with 6,381 additional claims; California, with 4,490; North Carolina, with 3,185; Kentucky, with 1,488; Georgia, with 1,246; and Puerto Rico, with 1,126.

New York cited additional layoffs in the service industries, California had increased layoffs in the service and motion picture industries and agriculture and Georgia reported more layoffs in the carpet industry.
North Carolina cited additional layoffs in the construction, textile and primary metals industry, while Kentucky had layoffs in the electrical equipment industry. Puerto Rico had no comment.
